title: Crowded Places
short: Population density is the number of people per square kilometer: divide the people by the land area.
trouble: Students confuse a large population with a high density. Bangladesh has fewer people than the United States but is far more crowded.

blocks.html: A country can have many people and still feel empty, or few people and feel crowded. To compare, we use population density: the number of people per square kilometer. It is a unit rate, like those in Unit Rates, built from a country's population and its area.
Population density = people ÷ land area. The answer is in people per square kilometer (people per km²).

Dividing shares the people out evenly: if 600 people live on 3 km², and they spread out evenly, each square kilometer has 600 ÷ 3 = 200 people. Real people are never spread evenly, so density is an average. It lets us compare a giant country and a tiny one fairly.

blocks.q: An island has 12,000 people on 40 km² of land. What is its population density?

blocks.title: Many people, but less crowded
blocks.q: Bangladesh has about 174 million people on about 148,000 km². The United States has about 345 million on about 9.8 million km². Which is more crowded?
steps: Bangladesh has half as many people but is more than 30 times as crowded.

blocks.html: A large population is not the same as a high density. Bangladesh has fewer people than the United States, but it is far more crowded, because they share much less land. Always divide by the area before you compare.
